bdx_001: You can recognise it by its three trunks fused near the ground into one sculptural mass, the thickest tree in the city's register. It stands in Parc Chantegrillon on Bordeaux's right bank.
bdx_006: You can recognise the pair by their near-identical girths, 393 and 390 centimetres, standing about ten metres apart. They stand in the same small garden as the register's black poplar, Parc Chantegrillon.
tok_014: You can recognise it by the eighty-two wooden props holding up its sideways-spreading limbs, wider than it is tall. It stands in the precinct of Zenyoji Temple, Edogawa-ku.
tok_015: You can recognise it by its trunk, forking into two limbs less than two metres off the ground with a root spread of 13.5 metres. It stands in the Konpira-do precinct of Myogyoji Temple, Saitama.
plg_001: You can recognise it by the lightning scar running down its trunk, the source of its name. It stands in the central part of Plunge Manor Park, beside the Oginskiai Palace.
plg_005: You can recognise it as hollow and without a crown, its top long gone, still standing beside the road. It stands in Viestovenai village, beside road 166 near the Viestove stream.
plg_006: You can recognise it by its trunk, reading as several stems grown into one with a distinct lump where legend places a witch's knot. It stands in Plateliai Manor Park, on the shore of Lake Plateliai.
stb_003: You can recognise the pair by their spring flowers, dense one-sided orange combs that turn the whole square that colour. They stand metres apart in Largo Marques de Pombal, on the former Praca de Sao Pedro.
stb_005: You can recognise the pair as survivors of the woodland that stood here before the street was built, one of them the thickest trunk in central Setubal. They stand on Rua Engenheiro Henri Perron.
stb_008: You can recognise the pair by their height, 25 metres, standing beside the Escola Secundaria do Bocage. They stand on Praceta Manuel Nunes de Almeida.
